Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexWave Communications Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.
I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexWave Communications's Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Jordan Hayes, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Network Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Commercial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team.
Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Jordan Hayes: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q4, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments.
Our key achievements include robust free cash flow generation of $8.7 billion for the full year, up 18% year-over-year, which exceeded guidance and fueled debt reduction, share repurchases, dividends, and tuck-in acquisitions. We made significant progress in our fiber buildout, passing 4.2 million homes with an additional 450,000 in the quarter, achieving a 27.4% take rate and 162,000 new subscribers. ARPU trends showed strength with blended postpaid ARPU at $58.42, up 4.8% year-over-year, thanks to pricing actions and bundling across mobile, broadband, and video. In enterprise and B2B, we posted $1.2 billion in revenue, up 28%, with key wins totaling over $850 million including major deals in banking, automotive, logistics, and public sector. Our spectrum assets reached 72% average utilization, with plans to refarm legacy holdings, pursue new auctions, and innovate via slicing for media and edge. We are guiding subscriber and revenue growth with Q1 net adds around 1.2 million and full-year 2025 revenue of $64.5 to $65.5 billion, up 7-8%. Capital expenditures for network investments are set at $13.8 to $14.5 billion for 2024, focused on 5G SA, fiber, and edge. Finally, net subscriber additions totaled 285,000, with 240,000 residential and 45,000 business, driven by fiber, 5G bundles, and enterprise wins.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Jordan. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $19.2 billion, reflecting a 5% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $8.1 billion, resulting in a margin of 42%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $2.4 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.
Good afternoon, everyone. As we wrap up a transformative year, I'd like to dive deep into our free cash flow—or FCF—generation and utilization, which remains the cornerstone of our financial strength and strategic flexibility in this capital-intensive telecom and media landscape. For the full year, we generated $8.7 billion in FCF, up 18% year-over-year and exceeding our guidance midpoint by $400 million. In Q4 alone, FCF came in at $2.4 billion, a robust 22% sequential increase from Q3, driven by seasonal EBITDA tailwinds and disciplined capex execution.
Let me break down the generation first. FCF, as you know, is our cash from operations minus capital expenditures. Operating cash flow hit a record $18.2 billion for the year, fueled by 5% adjusted EBITDA growth to $32.4 billion, or 42% of revenue—our highest margin in five years. Key drivers included wireless subscriber net adds of 4.2 million, primarily postpaid mobility, with ARPU expanding 3.8% to $58.50 on premium 5G Unlimited plans and device financing uptake. In our fixed broadband segment, FTTH penetration reached 62% of our footprint, delivering 4.2% revenue growth and sub-1% churn through bundling with our WaveStream SVOD service, which now boasts 28 million paid subscribers—closing the gap on pure-plays like Netflix.
We also saw meaningful working capital efficiencies, generating a $1.1 billion tailwind from optimized vendor terms and lower content prepayments amid normalizing streaming residuals post-strikes. Capex totaled $9.5 billion, or 12.3% of revenue, down 50 basis points YoY as our capex intensity normalized after peaking at 14% in 2022 during the height of our nationwide 5G Standalone core deployment. We deployed Open RAN architecture across 45% of our small cell sites in partnership with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony, reducing opex by 15-20% per site while accelerating mid-band C-band spectrum utilization from our 2021 FCC auction wins.
Regionally, North America—85% of our revenue—drove 75% of FCF at $6.5 billion, bolstered by enterprise 5G private networks for verticals like manufacturing and healthcare, akin to Verizon's momentum. Europe contributed $1.4 billion, flat YoY amid regulatory headwinds in Germany and the UK on wholesale pricing, but with upside from our 3.6 GHz spectrum holdings enabling fixed wireless access trials. APAC, via our 25% stake in IndiWave, added $800 million, up 25% on 5G monetization and data pricing discipline.
Turning to utilization, our $8.7 billion FCF deployment underscores our balanced capital allocation framework: invest for growth, delever, and return excess to shareholders. We prioritized debt reduction with $3.2 billion in repayments, bringing net debt to adjusted EBITDA to 2.1x—well below our 2.5x target and in line with deleveraging playbooks. This supports our A- stable outlook from S&P.
Shareholder returns totaled $4.1 billion: $2.5 billion in buybacks under our $10 billion authorization, retiring 4.1% of shares at an average $42, accretive to EPS by 8%; and $1.6 billion in dividends, with our quarterly payout raised 7% to $0.28 per share, yielding 2.8% forward. The balance, $1.4 billion, funded strategic tuck-ins, including our $900 million acquisition of MediaForge, a cloud gaming platform enhancing low-latency streaming over our edge CDN—critical in the console wars with Xbox Cloud and PlayStation Plus.
Looking ahead, we guide FY2024 FCF to $9.2-$9.8 billion, implying 6-13% growth, with capex at $9.0-$9.5 billion focused on 6G R&D pilots, AI-optimized network slicing, and rural broadband via BEAD funding. Trends like declining capex intensity to 11-12% of revenue, coupled with 3-4% EBITDA CAGR from 5G enterprise and converged media-wireless bundles, position us to sustain progressive dividend growth while pursuing bolt-on M&A in content and edge compute amid hyperscaler partnerships like AWS Outposts.
In summary, our FCF engine is firing on all cylinders, enabling us to navigate spectrum renewal cycles, content amortization pressures, and cord-cutting headwinds while outperforming peers on returns-adjusted growth.
I'll also touch on our capex guidance for network investments. For FY2024, we are guiding total network capex to the range of $13.8 billion to $14.5 billion, representing a modest 3% to 8% increase year-over-year from our $13.4 billion spend in 2023. This guidance reflects our disciplined approach to balancing aggressive network modernization with improving free cash flow generation—targeting $5.2 to $5.8 billion in FCF for the year, up from $4.7 billion last year.
Breaking it down: 43% or $5.9B to $6.3B to 5G SA and advanced wireless, including 15,000 small cells and upgrades for URLLC and FWA growth to 10 million subs by 2025; 32% or $4.4B to $4.7B to fiber-to-the-X, passing 25 million locations; 16% or $2.2B to $2.4B to edge computing and media delivery with 500 new PoPs; and 9% to spectrum and maintenance. North America drives 72%, with efficiencies from AI/ML cutting opex by $400 million annually.
For subscriber and revenue growth guidance: For Q1 2024, we expect total broadband equivalent subscribers to grow 2.5% to 3.0% quarter-over-quarter, or 1.2 million net adds—400k-450k wireless postpaid phones, 600k-700k fiber broadband, 200k-250k AstraStream video. For FY2025, 6-7% total subscriber growth or 5.5 million net adds.
Q1 revenue at $15.8B-$16.0B, up 5-6%; FY2025 consolidated $64.5B-$65.5B, up 7-8%, with wireless $35.5B +7%, broadband $17.0B +9%, media $8.5B +6%. This embeds $1.2B quarterly capex and EBITDA margins expanding to 47.5%.

Mike Thornton: Thank you. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage, delivering faster speeds and lower latency. Our network reliability remains high, and we are continuously optimizing our infrastructure to meet growing demand. We are also focusing on enhancing our cybersecurity posture. We are committed to pushing fiber and spectrum efficiencies.
On fiber buildout: In Q4, we passed an additional 450,000 homes, bringing our total fiber footprint to 4.2 million homes passed as of year-end. That's a 38% year-over-year increase and 12% quarter-over-quarter growth, on pace for 6.5 million by end-2024 toward 12 million by 2026, covering 15% of top 100 U.S. MSAs. Capex efficiency at $850 per home passed, down 15%, via micro-trenching reducing costs 20-25%.
Regionally: Northeast 1.8M HSP up 25% YoY; Midwest 1.1M leveraging overbuilds; Sunbelt 1.3M new in FL/TX/AZ. Over 70% new builds XGS-PON 10G symmetric, with 50G PON trials in Dallas tying to media bundles at 35% higher attach rates.
Customer adoption: 162,000 fiber subscribers added, total 1.15M at 27.4% take rate, up 300bps QoQ ahead of peers. Churn 0.8% monthly, 2Gig+ 42% of adds, ARPU +18% YoY. Q1 guidance: 500k HSP, 175k adds.
On spectrum assets: We hold 245 MHz average depth in top 100 U.S. markets—120 MHz 2.5 GHz, 100 MHz C-band, 25 MHz 600 MHz low-band, 800 MHz mmWave urban. Utilization at 72% busy-hour, up from 58% YoY on 42% 5G traffic surge.
By band: low-band 65% for rural FWA; mid-band 81% with 28% efficiency gain via 8x8 MIMO, 450 Mbps medians; mmWave 55% at 3.2 Gbps peaks. 5G 68% of data, video 55%.
Mitigated congestion via DSS reclaiming 15 MHz, $450M capex yielding 3.2x ROI, churn to 0.92%.
Future: Refarm 40 MHz 1.9 GHz PCS to 5G by YE24 to 285 MHz; target 60 MHz Auction 108 at $0.45/MHz-POP; NTN JV with AST; MIMO upgrades for 90% utilization; 10% C-band slicing for sports, $120M wholesale; mmWave for gaming. Positions for 15-18% wireless CAGR, margins to 48%.

Lisa Chen: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We've seen strong subscriber growth across our various service offerings. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, and we are continuously improving the customer experience. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships to offer bundled services and enhance customer value. We are prioritizing subscriber momentum and B2B expansion.
On ARPU trends: Blended postpaid ARPU $58.42, +4.8% YoY or $2.68 uplift. Mobile $49.27 +3.2% on Unlimited Plus 22% pen, $4-6 pricing in 85% markets; Northeast/West +4.1%, rural +2.9%. Broadband $67.85 +6.1% on fiber 42% pen, triple-play 68% at $12.40 inc ARPU; Europe +5.3%. Video $28.65 +1.9%, StreamHub 62% attach $4.20 uplift, LatAm +7.4%.
Pricing 45% of growth, bundling balance; lines/account 3.4. Q1 $59.10-$59.50 +4.5-5.0%.
Net subscriber additions: Q4 total 285,000 up 12% YoY, ninth straight sequential gain. Residential 240,000: 180k broadband on 350k homes passed, 45% pen; mobile postpaid 45k on 5G SA 75% coverage, Family Unlimited $58 ARPU; video 15k offset by streaming. U.S. 70%, Mexico JV 30k.
Business 45,000 +28% YoY: 30k SMB Ethernet/SD-WAN, 15k enterprise like Disney for AR/VR. ARPU $1,450 +11%, churn 0.7%.
Enterprise/B2B: $1.2B Q4 revenue +28% YoY 12% QoQ, 11th double-digit quarter. Connectivity $745M +32%, EdgeCloud $285M +45%, media $170M +15%.
Wins >$850M ACV: NA $250M bank 5G private, $45M retailer IoT; EMEA €120M auto V2X, £80M NHS; APAC $150M logistics IoT; LatAm $60M energy. 450 new customers YTD +60%, deal $8.5M +22%, churn 1.2%. Pipeline $4.2B +30%, FY $4.8-4.9B +27%, margins to 42%.
Q1 residential 220-250k, business 40-50k.

Raj Patel: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to transform our business. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations, improve customer service, and develop new products and services. We are also investing in research and development to stay ahead of the curve. Our technological direction is advancing Open RAN, network slicing, edge with AWS/Nokia, AI personalization, Wi-Fi 7, vOLT, and 50G PON for converged media-wireless leadership.

Emily Vargas: Thank you. Operationally, we are focused on improving efficiency and streamlining our processes. We are leveraging data analytics to optimize our resource allocation and improve decision-making. We are also committed to sustainability and reducing our environmental impact. Our operational focus is capex efficiency, working capital optimization, opex reductions via Open RAN/AI, 99.999% SLAs, and green bonds for fiber.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from John Miller with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Miller: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth?

Jordan Hayes: Thanks, John. Our content strategy centers on WaveStream SVOD and bundles like StreamHub with Peacock, Disney+, HBO Max, and Nexus Originals, driving 28 million paid subs and 35% attach rates on fiber. We're investing in originals akin to NFL exclusives, Premier League, Taylor Swift concerts, and FAST channels (100+), plus NBA League Pass. This offsets linear declines, boosts video ARPU +1.9% to $28.65, and lifts blended ARPU 12% via 65% wireless bundle take. Anticipated impact: 200k-250k Q1 video adds, FY2025 media revenue $8.5B +6%, total subs +6-7% or 5.5M net adds, churn to 1.8% with AI recommendations.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve fiber penetration targets?

Lisa Chen: Great question, Emily. We're tackling the digital divide via FiberFirst in Sunbelt/Midwest greenfields and rural via BEAD subsidies ($800M grants), RDOF, low-cost green bonds $2.2B, and FWA on low-band spectrum 85% take in Midwest. FTTH to 25M locations by 2024-end, 65% serviceable addresses 2025, with $850/home efficiency. Affordable bundles at $79.99 with streaming, gigabit 85% adoption. Achieve targets: 500k Q1 HSP, 175k adds, 27.4% take rate via Wi-Fi 7 mesh, 92% retention, outpacing AT&T/Verizon rural.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including share buybacks and dividends?

Sarah Kline: Absolutely, David. Priorities: growth investments like fiber/5G/edge, delever to 2.1x net debt/EBITDA, then shareholder returns. FY2023 FCF $8.7B utilized $3.2B debt paydown, $2.5B buybacks (4.1% shares at $42, +8% EPS), $1.6B dividends (+7% to $0.28/share, 2.8% yield), $1.4B tuck-ins like $900M MediaForge. FY2024 FCF $9.2-9.8B supports $3B buybacks, 4-6% dividend growth, bolt-ons. Balanced framework sustains amid spectrum/content pressures.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Patel: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

Jordan Hayes: Thanks, Rachel. We're proactively engaging FCC on net neutrality, broadband labels, Auction 108 (target 60 MHz 3.45GHz), BEAD/RDOF subsidies. In Europe, navigating Ofcom/EU Gigabit Act, DMA bundling probes, GDPR for edge. UK/Germany wholesale pricing headwinds mitigated via convergence JVs like Vodafone. Spectrum refarming/JVs like AST NTN for rural. Compliance via A- ratings, sovereign cloud mandates. Positions us for 15-20% enterprise 5G/edge share by 2026.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Jordan, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Jordan Hayes: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
